statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail falls to 18% because the break to 28,927.50 was fully retraced, NQ is back within about 20 points of the 29,125.50 close, VIX has slipped to 16.09 near its session low and the 2Y, 10Y and 30Y all eased after ADP printed 38K against a 47K consensus. Stress stays high at 68% on crude near six-week highs and a 10Y that touched its highest level since November 2023 earlier today.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, reflecting observed two-way price discovery rather than an improvement in the macro backdrop. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 13:00-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open, Factory Orders and the EIA report, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom call. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures fully retrace the break to 28,927.50 as a 38K ADP print eases yields and VIX slides to 16.09
body: NQ futures traded at 29,101.50 to 29,105.00 shortly after 12:18 UTC across two independent quotes, down 20.50 to 24.00 points or roughly 0.07% to 0.08% from the 29,125.50 previous close. The structural change from the previous cycle is decisive. An hour ago price sat at 29,016.50, about 89 points off a session low of 28,927.50 that had just been marked; since then the low has held and the index has recovered roughly 175 points from it, leaving the day range at 28,927.50 to 29,170.00 and price back in the upper half of that range near unchanged. A marginal new low that is then fully retraced is the opposite of repeated extension after failed pullbacks, and it is the primary reason Tail falls to 18% from 20%. Three cross-checks support the reading rather than contradict it. First, ADP private payrolls printed 38,000 for August at 12:15 UTC against a 47,000 consensus and an upwardly revised 46,000 prior, and the reaction was orderly: the 2-year is 4.39%, down 2.4 basis points, the 10-year 4.78%, down 1.8 basis points from an intraday 4.82% that marked the highest level since November 2023, and the 30-year 5.25%, down 2.9 basis points. Second, VIX is 16.09, down 1.53% from a 16.34 close and sitting at the bottom of a 16.06 to 16.82 session range, so the volatility impulse observed earlier has decayed rather than built. Third, WTI is 89.70, down 0.57%, with Brent at 94.28, down 0.39%; both remain close to six-week highs on the US-Iran escalation around the Strait of Hormuz, but neither is extending today. Against that, the prior session's composition was uniformly negative in the parts of the market that matter most for this index, with all seven tracked semiconductors lower at a mean of -1.06% and only one of eight megacaps higher, and the policy backdrop remains hawkish despite the soft labour print. That combination keeps Stress high at 68% while the observed intraday path maps Tail into the low band. The narrow danger window spans 13:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC cash open, the 14:00 UTC Factory Orders release and the 14:30 UTC EIA report. Nothing beyond ADP has printed at the assessment cutoff, and no post-open structure is asserted.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours opened with Tail elevated at 28% and peaking at 31% around the 1 September US cash open, as the US-Iran escalation, the crude surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in. Tail then decayed through the US afternoon and the Asian handover and has held a 20-25% band for the last twenty published hours, with the dominant mode rotating from event/whipsaw to trend-down during this morning's European session. Stress stayed persistently high in a 70-77% range throughout. That profile describes a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend, and this cycle's full retracement of the session low is consistent with it. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low and watch bands for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the two-hour catalyst cluster from 13:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the US cash open, Factory Orders and the EIA report, plus one further hour at 21:00 UTC around the Broadcom results and call, where a top-weight semiconductor constituent can move the complex in a thin post-close book. The Beige Book at 18:00 UTC is treated as a single-hour checkpoint inside the watch band. Stress stays high throughout on the crude, sovereign-yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday, and eases only gradually through the Asian session before rebuilding into the 3 September European morning ahead of Challenger, jobless claims, ISM Services and Friday's payrolls. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.
